notes:
High-level: Northbridge builds a VS Code copilot extension aimed at teams (internal devs + customers). They need a low-latency streaming backend that can power inline suggestions and live completions with <100ms/per-token ideal and 50–150ms acceptable.

What they told us / asks: 
- "Prefer hosted API for speed to market, but Dedicated or VPC for customer-facing tiers; will evaluate Private if SAML/residency required."
- "We need explicit model/version pinning per extension release — can't roll to a new model without CI gating + offline fallback."
- Streaming requirements: server-driven incremental tokens (server-stream) + client-side debounce to avoid duplicate calls. They care about prefix caching (popular repo prompts) and local KV cache to reduce tokens.
- Rate limiting: per-developer and per-organization token caps. They want an SLA/guarantee for 'burst' days (hackathon spikes) and clear 429 behavior.
- Observability: require token-level latency histograms, per-endpoint token cost breakdown, and per-suggestion confidence scores for telemetry.
- Security: Okta SSO/SAML mandatory for admin console; audit logs retention 1yr; optional KMS for key wrapping; data residency for EU customers.

POC scope (agreed): 
- 2-week pilot with 25 internal devs using VS Code extension connected to Redwood hosted endpoint; collect latency + token usage.
- Test model pinning (pin Llama-3/quantized variant) and fallback to smaller quantized model for cold starts.
- Validate streaming UX (start-to-first-token, token cadence) and extension-level error handling for 429/503.

Sales notes / friction: 
- Legal asking for sub-processors list and DPA changes for customer-facing product.
- AppSec wants extension package scan results and a reproducible way to sign extension builds.
- Engineering asked: "Can we get a per-user rate-limit header and token bucket peek in responses?" — we should provide example headers.

Quotes / call snippets: 
- "We need inline suggestions to feel instantaneous — devs will reject anything >150ms." — Head of Product
- "If we can pin a model per release and certify it, we’d avoid regressions during extension updates." — Engineering lead

Open technical questions (to resolve in POC): 
- How does Redwood expose token-level billing to the client SDK for offline cost attribution?
- SLO for streaming first-byte latency across regions (NA/EU) — do we provide region routing policies?
- Behavior for rate-limited streams: reconnect/backoff patterns recommended?

Next immediate asks (action items): 
- Provide POC onboarding doc + quickstart VS Code extension sample (token streaming).
- Share security pack (SOC2, ISO certs) and sub-processor list.
- Draft dedicated capacity quote for 100k tokens/day baseline + burst policy.

Contact: Head of Product — Maya R. (maya.r@northbridge-ide.com), Eng Lead — Tom Keller (tom.k@northbridge-ide.com)
